verdict: Cost per lead improving, but lead volume remains too thin to scale.
narrative: Over the last 28 days, your cost per lead came in at $235.23 across 10 tracked leads — a high unit cost, though the most recent 7-day window shows that number falling 18.65% compared to the prior 7 days, which is a directionally good sign. Google Ads spend increased sharply week-over-week, which drove the 28-day average up, but early conversion data suggests the campaign is beginning to find its footing. The priority right now is confirming your lead intake is staffed and responsive before any further budget increases are made — speed to answer is a direct multiplier on what paid campaigns can deliver. Once intake coverage is confirmed, we are positioned to push spend back up with more confidence behind it.

highlights.phrase: cost per lead over the last 28 days, trending down 18.65% in the most recent 7-day period
tracked leads received this period across all paid channels
actions taken on your Google Business Profile this period — calls, direction requests, and website clicks

watch_item.issue: Lead intake coverage is unconfirmed, meaning new leads may not be reached quickly enough to convert — this is the single largest constraint on growth right now.
watch_item.fix: Budget increases are paused until an intake owner is confirmed; once that seat is filled, the scale-up process resumes immediately.
